the spell that duplicates a disaster duplicates its effect, the raise water flood example; the major-disaster DM judgment that could annihilate a realm; the ripe areas noted when the maps are prepared), the accidental causes (only the frailest locations, triggered by the weight of a creature walking or by sounds, the DM-assigned percentage by weakness, the 5% ledge example modified when laden or accompanied by mules, the doubled chance when running, the melee doubling with all participating weights figured carefully for nonhumans, the reduced chance when the weak area is not directly beneath with sound the only other avenue, the sound chance by loudness and sharpness with the no-chance conversation and the 1% sword-clash examples), the excavation causes (digging away a significant ceiling support, mining the most common cause, the shoring precaution with the mining-rules seam, the escape-tunnel and rubble-clearing risk of about double the accidental chance, the 10% per turn), the sabotage causes (the opportune collapse, the collapses on the saboteurs themselves, the accessible targets - the columns, bridge supports and narrow rock layers against the soaring ceiling - the miner-proficiency requirement, the sixths splits without and with the proficiency, the considerable time and noise with the page-50 excavation-rules seam), and the random occurrences (the chance growing with extended underground time, the 1% per day base, the 10% per 10 days long-expedition option, the cave-in near the PCs but not on top of them or within earshot, the Table 17 cross-reference, the movement-relative directions, the higher roll the farther away, the possibly-undiscovered cave-in and the decayed-stone or rotten-timber double-or-triple increase).

consts.name: dnwSabotageNoMinerSuccessSixths
consts.comment: a character without miner proficiency who makes a sabotage attempt has a 1/3 chance of successfully completing his task - 2 of 6.

consts.name: dnwSabotageNoMinerTooStrongSixths
consts.comment: without miner proficiency, a 1/3 chance of leaving the structure too strong to collapse - 2 of 6.

consts.name: dnwSabotageNoMinerSelfCollapseSixths
consts.comment: without miner proficiency, a 1/3 chance of bringing the structure down upon himself - 2 of 6.

consts.name: dnwSabotageMinerSuccessSixths
consts.comment: a character with miner proficiency has a 2/3 chance of successfully sabotaging the area - 4 of 6.

consts.name: dnwSabotageMinerUnderdamageSixths
consts.comment: with miner proficiency, a 1/6 chance of not damaging the structure enough - 1 of 6.

consts.name: dnwSabotageMinerSelfCollapseSixths
consts.comment: with miner proficiency, a 1/6 chance of damaging it so extensively that it collapses during the sabotage attempt - 1 of 6.

consts.name: dnwAccidentalLedgeExamplePct
consts.comment: a ledge might have eroded to the point where it has a 5% chance of collapsing per character crossing it (the djvu garble 596, settled by the Acrobat layer).

consts.name: dnwSwordClashCollapsePctPerRound
consts.comment: the clashing of swords in combat might give a 1% chance per round of a cave-in on a sound-fragile area (the djvu garble 196).

consts.name: dnwExcavationCollapsePctPerTurn
consts.comment: there is about a 10% chance per turn that a weakened ceiling or tunnel wall collapses during excavation (the djvu garble 1096).

consts.name: dnwExcavationChanceMult
consts.comment: the possibility of a cave-in while digging an escape tunnel or clearing rubble is about double that of an accidental cave-in.

consts.name: dnwRandomCaveInPctPerDay
consts.comment: the base chance for a cave-in during underground exploration is 1% per day.

consts.name: dnwRandomCaveInLongExpeditionPct
consts.comment: on long expeditions the DM may wish to alter the daily roll to a 10% chance.

consts.name: dnwRandomCaveInLongExpeditionDays
consts.comment: the long-expedition cave-in roll is made every 10 days.

consts.name: dnwDecayedChanceMultMax
consts.comment: in areas of exceptionally decayed stone or rotten supporting timbers, such considerations could double, or perhaps triple, the chance of a randomly occurring cave-in.

consts.name: dnwRunChanceMult
consts.comment: the chance of collapse may be doubled if the characters run across a weakened ledge, since the pounding is much harder than when walking slowly.

consts.name: dnwMeleeChanceMult
consts.comment: the chance of collapse should be doubled for melee combat on a fragile surface, because of the additional pounding the surface takes.

consts.name: dnwT17RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 17 carries eight location bands: on top, immediately in front, immediately behind, in front within hearing, behind within hearing, well behind out of hearing, well in front out of hearing, and the entrance.

bools.name: dnwCaveInUniqueToUnderground
bools.comment: cave-ins are unique to the underground environment.

bools.name: dnwConsideredWhenStressingRock
bools.comment: the chance that the roof of an underground location may cave in must be considered especially if characters are excavating, using explosive magic, or otherwise placing stress on the overhanging rock.

bools.name: dnwBridgeFloorAlsoEndanger
bools.comment: cave-ins can also endanger characters in other ways: a bridge being crossed may collapse, or a floor may give way, dropping those standing on it amid tons of jagged, crushing rock.

bools.name: dnwTriggerAsAttackChainRisk
bools.comment: characters may try to trigger a cave-in as a means of attacking an enemy; such attempts must be made cautiously, since a cave-in may create a chain reaction that collapses a far larger area than intended.

bools.name: dnwStrongStructureOnlyDisasters
bools.comment: a strong cavern, dungeon, or realm is only susceptible to cave-ins as a result of natural disasters such as floods, earthquakes, or volcanic eruptions.

bools.name: dnwSpellDuplicatesDisaster
bools.comment: certain magical spells that duplicate natural disasters can duplicate their destructive effects; a raise water spell that creates a flood in a tunnel should be treated as a natural flood.

bools.name: dnwMajorDisasterDmJudgment
bools.comment: in the case of a major natural disaster the DM's judgment determines the exact area of effect; the far-reaching effects of a major earthquake might actually annihilate an entire subterranean realm.

bools.name: dnwRipeAreasNotedOnMaps
bools.comment: underground areas ripe for cave-ins - aging or recent-disaster-weakened, needing only a slight additional pressure - should be noted when the maps for an underground area are prepared.

bools.name: dnwAccidentalOnlyFrailest
bools.comment: only the frailest of underground locations are susceptible to accidental cave-ins.

bools.name: dnwAccidentalWeightOrSound
bools.comment: accidental collapses are triggered by the weight of a creature walking across a weak spot, or even by the sounds created by characters or creatures.

bools.name: dnwDmAssignsCollapsePct
bools.comment: based on the weakness of the area under consideration, the DM should assign a percentage chance of a collapse occurring.

bools.name: dnwLadenOrBeastsModifyPct
bools.comment: the collapse chance should be modified if the characters are very heavily laden, or accompanied by mules or other creatures.

bools.name: dnwRunDoublesChance
bools.comment: the chance of collapse may be doubled if the characters run across a weakened surface.

bools.name: dnwMeleeDoublesChance
bools.comment: if characters participate in melee combat on a fragile surface, the weight of all participating creatures must be figured in - carefully, for nonhuman creatures such as ogres - and the chance of collapse should be doubled.

bools.name: dnwOffPositionReducedChance
bools.comment: where the weakened area is not directly beneath the characters, the chance of a cave-in is reduced; unless the characters apply weight to the area, sound is the only other likely avenue for causing an accidental collapse.

bools.name: dnwSoundChanceByLoudness
bools.comment: the intensity of the sound must be considered, with a percentage chance of collapse assigned according to the loudness and sharpness of the noise; an area might stand no chance under normal conversation but the clashing of swords might give a 1% chance per round.

bools.name: dnwExcavationRisksSupport
bools.comment: whenever characters or creatures are digging into the earth, they run the risk of excavating away a significant support for the ceiling, causing a cave-in.

bools.name: dnwMiningMostCommonCause
bools.comment: mining is the most common cause of excavation cave-ins, and precautions such as shoring up an excavated passage are usually taken by the miners - the mining-rules seam.

bools.name: dnwUnshoredEscapeTunnelRisk
bools.comment: characters digging an escape tunnel or clearing rubble from a previous cave-in are often unable to properly shore up their excavated passage; weakened surfaces then stand a fair chance of collapsing.

bools.name: dnwSabotageNeedsMinerProficiency
bools.comment: to chip stone away to the point where a collapse is likely requires some skill at stonework and a little luck; a character must have miner proficiency to have a decent chance of successfully sabotaging an underground area.

bools.name: dnwSabotageMayCrushSaboteur
bools.comment: many areas subject to sabotage collapse on the heads of the saboteurs themselves.

bools.name: dnwSabotageTargetsAccessible
bools.comment: columns that support a ceiling, bridge supports, or narrow layers of rock walked over are obvious sabotage targets; the soaring ceiling of a vast chamber is very difficult to damage, while its supporting columns are much more accessible.

bools.name: dnwSabotageTimeAndNoise
bools.comment: sabotage attempts take considerable time and create quite a bit of noise; see the excavation rules for how long it might take to chisel through a column - the page-50 seam.

bools.name: dnwRandomChanceGrowsWithTime
bools.comment: if a campaign focuses on the underground for extended periods, the chance of a naturally occurring cave-in affecting the characters increases.

bools.name: dnwRandomMeansNearNotOnTop
bools.comment: a successful random-occurrence roll means a cave-in has occurred somewhere in the underground region near the PCs - not on top of the characters, and not necessarily within their earshot.

bools.name: dnwT17RelativeToMovement
bools.comment: all Table 17 directions relate to the party's direction of movement at the time of the cave-in.

bools.name: dnwHigherRollFartherAway
bools.comment: in the categories indicating a cave-in some distance away, the higher the roll, the farther away the cave-in.

bools.name: dnwCaveInMayGoUndiscovered
bools.comment: it is quite possible for a group of characters to fail to discover a cave-in that occurs during their adventures.

bools.name: dnwDecayedStoneChanceIncrease
bools.comment: in areas of exceptionally decayed stone, or of rotten supporting timbers, the DM may increase the chance of a randomly occurring cave-in - possibly doubling or tripling it.

bools.name: dnwExcavationChanceAboutDouble
bools.comment: the possibility of a cave-in while digging without proper shoring is about double that of an accidental cave-in, with about a 10% chance per turn of a weakened ceiling or tunnel wall collapsing.
